data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Aġlab at taʕle, an arnuwwe maḏəriwo aw warze ġalabe.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: Mostly the foxes, the rabbits would harm the vegetable plots a great deal.

rationale: First Infectum-wa 1; explicit plural animals and crop patients in a short habitual clause. No new crop-damage sense.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.50/2485)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Kətwo mərmərkat, kito masala hno pərpayrat, kito masayəl hawxa ġalabe... E pərpayrat, kito masayəl dədwone hawxa rabe maḏəriwo u sawal, hala maḏəriwo aw warze, u kətono, maḏəriwo am masayəlani. Hani i ṭabiʕiyaṯṯe hawxa yo.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: There were mermirkat, there are, for example, what are they, butterflies, there are many such things... Yes, butterflies, there are such things, big worms that would harm the livestock, or harm the vegetable plots, the cotton, harm these things. This is their nature.

rationale: Infectum-wa 1 remains thin; livestock, crops and cotton occur as affected themes of the same verb. One quotation covers its three printed repetitions.

data.turoyo: Bəṯr mu Sayfo bu Madənḥo kule kḥuzena u ʕamayḏan, mede maḏ̣ərono aw mede mhaddədono, laḥ ḥəkmat dad dəwal, d ʕayiši bənne, lawəlle.
data.translation: After the Sayfo, throughout the East, we see that our people have become neither something harmful nor something threatening to the governments of the states in which they live.

rationale: First Part act. 1 maḏ̣ərono: -ono adjective with an affected laḥ-government phrase in written political argument; retain the participial/lexical boundary as a question.

summary: All eleven tokens retain III.1 schaden; no new lexical sense, Detransitive or collocation is supported. The plural and inanimate causes do not create participant-specific senses.

Preterit agents may be l-marked and indexed in -la, while the human patient can be a zero-marked NP. Infectum patients appear as bound suffixes, independent pronouns or l-marked NPs; neither affected pronouns nor source spelling establish Detransitive morphology.

Source ḏ, z and glossary ḏ̣ spellings are retained verbatim; the harm context distinguishes this homonym from ḏ̣yr 1 suckling. r+l assimilation is visible in gmaḏ̣əllan (113/160), without requiring a new sense.

Null sense numbers in inherited examples are counted under the only inherited sense 1 for the human layout; no inherited text is silently rewritten. The obviously prospective d maḏǝr clause is moved out of Preterit.
Round 1 moved the prospective d maḏǝr example to Infectum; after that move and additions, Preterit has two and Infectum five examples. That correction is retained as baseline and not repeated.
ḏ, ḏ̣ and source spellings remain verbatim. The harming contexts distinguish this root from the suckling homonym.

Infectum-wa expresses recurring crop/livestock damage. Written maḏ̣ərono is predicated negatively of a people and takes an affected government phrase, rather than asserting that the people caused actual harm.
Confirm the dialectal ḏ/ḏ̣/z correspondences and the supplied ending in lə+k̬maze<nna>; no reconstructed base form is published from that incomplete token.
94/221 German adds oder doch ohne nutzen without a counterpart in komaḏ̣iri. Does the wider edition context justify this addition? No harmless/useless meaning is inferred.
The inherited notes abruptly introduce farq/soyəm farq and a frq cross-reference, plus isolated f. Editors should check the Word boundary before relocating this material.

Does maḏ̣ərono in Jan 3.10/110 belong productively in the glossary’s Part act. box or only among lexical derivatives? Its -ono morphology and harm meaning are clear; the category boundary remains open.
The inherited isolated f and farq boundary issue remains for the editors from round 1; Jan evidence does not authorize relocation.
Harm extends to vegetable plots, cotton and livestock, and to community/town patients with political or institutional causes; no meaning split follows from participant changes.
